classification.difficultyReason: Recognise and apply nine successive right-triangle calculations, retaining exact surds.

content.prompt: Determine the value of $h$ in exact surd form.

spec.description: Nine successive right-angled triangles share a central vertex. The initial radius and all nine outer sides are labelled 1. Every outer junction has a right-angle marker, and the final radius is labelled h.
spec.mathematics: Starting with P0=(1,0), derive Pn=P(n−1)+(-y,x)/sqrt(x²+y²). Each new outer side has length 1 and is perpendicular to the preceding radius. The final radius has squared length 10.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and h are visible; intermediate radii and the final answer appear in controlled answers.

answer.worked:
Each outer unit side is perpendicular to the preceding radius. Let $r_1,\ldots,r_8$ be the successive intermediate radii. Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}
r_1&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\\
r_2&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{3}\\
r_3&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{4}=2\\
r_4&=\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt{5}\\
r_5&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}\\
r_6&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{6})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{7}\\
r_7&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{7})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{8}\\
r_8&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{8})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{9}=3\\
h&=\sqrt{3^2+1^2}=\sqrt{10}
\end{align*}$$
